---
title: "Pay native staging candidate"
description: "Qualify Pay on the shared Start bridge without live payment activity."
---

Pay retains its Next.js publisher and adds a TanStack Start/Void candidate. It
consumes the shared bridge, page adapter, action transport and internal API
resolver. The conversion adds no database migration, payment job or schedule.
A source build is not payment-provider acceptance or production cutover.

## Use root-only staging

The candidate admits `pay-staging.tuturuuu.com` and `pay.tuturuuu.com` as host
roots. It rejects apex mounts and unknown hosts before app code. The first
release targets `pay.tuturuuu.com`; apex hosting remains held by the shared auth
guard. Pay consumes the bridge's shared session model without a per-app cookie.

`cloudflare/staging-profile.json` owns the staging values used by Void, artifact
qualification and runtime checks. It pins Pay to `https://pay-staging.tuturuuu.com`,
Web/API to `https://staging.tuturuuu.com`, the repository's staging Supabase
project, and `POLAR_SANDBOX=true`. Supply only sandbox Polar credentials. The
artifact helper rejects a missing or false sandbox flag. This staging-data
artifact cannot be admitted as a production profile.

Every response sends noindex, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff and the strict-origin
referrer policy. CSP includes `frame-ancestors 'none'`. Personalized SSR and API
responses use private/no-store caching and vary on Cookie, Authorization and
Accept-Language. Only successful GET/HEAD compiled-asset responses keep their
static caching. `global_fetch_strictly_public` is required; hosted acceptance
must show same-zone self-fetches reach the Worker rather than retained Vercel.

## Preserve route and payment authority

The source inventory has six pages, one server-action module and 26 local API
handlers. Local billing, payment, webhook and existing job routes retain their
ownership; unmatched APIs forward to Web. Conversion does not authorize invoking
migration/job endpoints or changing provider webhook routing.

Exact GET/HEAD `/api/build-info` are public deployment identity reads. Their
ambient credentials are removed, and the shared guard remains in place. Other
methods and lookalike paths retain session checks. Polar webhook POSTs and the
existing cron GETs retain their handler signature/secret checks and shared edge
protection; no scheduler is enabled by the candidate.

## Qualify the emitted artifact

Run the exact-head unit, Next/Cloudflare types, lint, real `vp build`, registry
and route-tree checks, binding harness, emitted config and Wrangler dry-run on
Sonha through `ttr resources run`. Seal the output with
`scripts/ci/pay-native-artifact.py`, transfer it through the M4, and run both the
transferred and roundtrip-restored artifact on Thanh under browser admission.
Run `bun check:changed` before publication. The M4 runs no builds or containers.

The native workflow calls the shared qualification template. The generated raw
Host suite consumes declared root/login/dashboard outcomes from
`start-bridge.routes.json`. The app-owned runtime checks public build identity,
negative API controls, response security, staging auth-return origin, invalid
webhook rejection, missing cron authority, root-only host rejection and bounded
CDP-fenced Chromium navigation. All outbound database/provider requests are
blocked in these fixtures. This is not hosted shared-session, checkout or
payment-provider acceptance.

## Require provider sandbox acceptance

Before staging sign-off, record the sandbox account, exact Worker source/version,
profile/bindings and test identities through the release owner. Exercise:

- EN/VI signed-in workspace billing and permission denial across workspaces.
- Checkout completion and cancellation, credit packs and subscription changes.
- Valid signed webhook delivery, invalid signature rejection and replay handling.
- Seat changes, invoice delivery, billing details and the customer portal.
- Auth verification, refresh, logout and same-zone self-fetch on hosted staging.

Use disposable sandbox records and the original operation identity for any
uncertain write. Stop on an unknown outcome; do not replay blindly. No live
payments, production Polar credentials or live webhook reconfiguration are
admitted by these checks.

After independent review and hosted acceptance, the release owner's explicit
cutover-prep PR admits the production artifact/bindings and legacy-publisher hold.
The direct root-mode cutover needs a captured immutable Vercel deployment, DNS
payload and one-step rollback, followed by smoke and a 30–60 minute 5xx/auth/p95
watch. Production stays held until those gates pass.
